More critically, they concluded Bob can guarantee all 30 coins by guessing (2,11,17), which is impossible because Bob must assign guesses to boxes without knowing their counts; these guesses can exceed actual contents in valid distributions (e.g., 12,6,12), yielding zero from some boxes.
